names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 10 mai, «Sfântul Mucenic Filadelf».

Read out of saint.gr's line for 10 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Αλφειός, Κυπρίνος και Φιλάδελφος οι Αυτάδελφοι Μάρτυρες», with the rank word left off; the page's own head line for him is «Αγιος Φιλαδελφος ο Μαρτυρας».

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 10 May, „Свети мученици Алфеј, Филаделф и Кирин.“ — Свети left off, which is not a rank, and мученици left off, which is the `martyr` this folder already carries in `types`. One rank word stands over all three names and belongs to none of them; the heading gives no epithet, no city and no year. A direct walk of every `names` entry in `saints/` finds no folder holding Филаделф, so the form folds with nothing, although the corpus keeps two other Philadelphi — the martyr and the venerable of 8 February — neither of whom has a Serbian form.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 10 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Filadelf»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 10ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Αλφειός, Κυπρίνος και Φιλάδελφος οι Αυτάδελφοι Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 10 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps him, and he is the first of the three named in the page's own head lines. **`dates` are added where the folder had none**, as the reign the page prints. **The Greek adds** the brotherhood, the father Vitalius, the country of the Vascones in southern Italy, the baptism by a venerable man named Onesimus, the arrest by Anengelion, the sending bound to Rome, the governor Diomedes at Puteoli, Tertyllus the ruler of Sicily, and his own death: they burned him upon a red-hot gridiron. **`related` rows are added** for his two brothers and for `erasmus-10-may` and `onesimus-10-may`, whose page joins the five. **He is none of the corpus's other Philadelphi or the day's `philemon-disciple-of-passarion`**, who is another man on the same day. No relics, no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 23.05.2026 (10. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Алфеј, Филаделф и Кирин.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, an enumerated company of three, so one row each, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek both keep them on. **THE REIGN IS A DIFFERENT EMPEROR AND THE DATE WAS NOT TOUCHED**: „у време цара Ликинија“ against saint.gr's „επί αυτοκράτορα Δεκίου (249-251 μ.Χ.)“, and the Prologue gives Licinius with no bounds, which the coordinator's standing refusal of a boundless reign will not let a reader turn into an interval or use to widen one. `dates` unchanged, the disagreement recorded here and in the life. **His own death agrees exactly**: „Филаделф сажежен на гвозденој леси“ — burned on an iron grid — is saint.gr's red-hot gridiron, so that much is corroboration and not news. **New here**: the brothers born of one womb, the father a certain prince Vitalis in southern Italy, the nobility and the strength in the faith, the leading from judge to judge and torturer to torturer, the crossing into Sicily; **the finding of their incorrupt relics in 1517**, a date for the relics and not for the man, so it is in the life and not in `dates`; and **the appearance of the three brothers to Saint Euthalia**, „(в. 2. март)“, which `related_add` answers with a row in each direction. **The father Vitalis takes nothing**: the corpus's four Vitalis folders were read and he is none of them, so by the coordinator's third ruling no folder is minted and he is named instead. **No `locations`**. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr gives a reign and no year: «συνελήφθηκαν από τον Ανηγγελίωνα επί αυτοκράτορα Δεκίου (249-251 μ.Χ.)». The interval is that reign as the page prints it.
